ordered_diagnoses: Short-lasting Unilateral Neuralgiform Headache with Conjunctival Injection and Tearing (SUNCT) Syndrome

s1.syndrome_frame: Sudden onset of severe, episodic, unilateral facial pain with trigeminal nerve distribution, triggered by specific movements
salient_findings: Severe, electric-shock–like pain on the left side of the face
Pain localized to the V2 and V3 distributions of the left trigeminal nerve
Allodynia to cold air and hypersensitivity to touch in the affected area
key_facts: 36-year-old woman
Received third dose of Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine
Pain started the day after vaccination
Pain is episodic, sharp, and electric-shock–like
Pain is triggered by jaw movement during eating or tooth brushing
Pain reaches 10/10 on a numeric pain scale
Attacks last 4–5 seconds
Distorted sensations in the V2 region during attacks
Sensory testing is otherwise normal
No other neurological deficits
No relevant past medical or family history
Routine laboratory tests, including D-dimer, are normal
RT-qPCR for SARS-CoV-2 and other infections is negative
Contrast-enhanced MRI of the head shows no abnormalities

shortlist: Short-lasting Unilateral Neuralgiform Headache with Conjunctival Injection and Tearing (SUNCT) Syndrome

shortlist.label: Trigeminal Neuralgia
shortlist.why_kept: Episodic, sharp, electric-shock–like pain in the trigeminal nerve distribution, triggered by jaw movement

shortlist.label: Trigeminal Neuroma
shortlist.why_kept: Unilateral facial pain with trigeminal nerve distribution, possibility of a tumor compressing the nerve

shortlist.label: Short-lasting Unilateral Neuralgiform Headache with Conjunctival Injection and Tearing (SUNCT) Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Sudden onset of severe, episodic, unilateral facial pain with autonomic features

shortlist.label: Glossopharyngeal Neuralgia
shortlist.why_kept: Severe, episodic pain in the face and head, possibility of involvement of the glossopharyngeal nerve

shortlist.label: Postherpetic Neuralgia
shortlist.why_kept: Severe, persistent pain after a viral infection, possibility of herpes zoster reactivation

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of episodic, sharp, electric-shock–like pain in the V2 and V3 distributions of the left trigeminal nerve, triggered by jaw movement, are characteristic of Trigeminal Neuralgia.

rejected.label: Trigeminal Neuroma
rejected.why: There is no evidence of a tumor on the contrast-enhanced MRI of the head

rejected.label: Short-lasting Unilateral Neuralgiform Headache with Conjunctival Injection and Tearing (SUNCT) Syndrome
rejected.why: The patient does not exhibit conjunctival injection or tearing, which are hallmark symptoms of SUNCT Syndrome

rejected.label: Glossopharyngeal Neuralgia
rejected.why: The pain is localized to the V2 and V3 distributions of the trigeminal nerve, not the glossopharyngeal nerve

rejected.label: Postherpetic Neuralgia
rejected.why: There is no history of herpes zoster infection, which is a prerequisite for Postherpetic Neuralgia
